A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Fixed-Point RNN research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison despite extensive reorganization and renaming.

before.justification: v1 reports original state-tracking, copying and modular-arithmetic experiments, including ablations and fixed-point convergence analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original toy-task experiments and reports additional mixer comparisons, longer-sequence evaluations, training-time measurements and FineWeb language modeling results.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming Bedouin to FP-Mamba, v2 introduces Kronecker and diagonal-plus-low-rank mixers and an FP-Mamba2 adaptation. Appendix C.2 replaces v1's Griffin-style gate parametrization with original Mamba gating and per-iteration output normalization; Section 4.2 places the GLU inside the iteration. Appendix B.4 adds stopping after a batch convergence percentage and adaptive damped updates. These are substantive procedural changes, although some implementation descriptions conflict.

E1.justification: v2 adds natural-language modeling on FineWeb, extending evaluation beyond v1's synthetic tasks. A5, S5, copying and bracketed modular arithmetic remain covered. Longer versions of the retained state-tracking tasks primarily change evaluation settings.

E2.justification: v2 adds DeltaProduct to the long-sequence state-tracking comparison in Figure 9 and GatedDeltaProduct to the modular-arithmetic comparison in Table 2. The existing principal comparator families remain; Siems et al. was already cited in v1.

E3.justification: For retained state tracking, the reported sample count changes from 1.6M to 16M and batch size from 128 to 512; v2 also specifies 500k test sequences. New experiments train at length 128 and evaluate through 512, measure training time on common hardware, and evaluate 12-layer, width-768 language models at context length 2048. The copying comparison reports four-layer GatedDeltaNet in v1 Figure 4 versus two layers in v2 Figure 5.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 3 adds vector-state mixer and hidden-feedback comparisons with convergence counts. Figures 4–5 expand mixer analyses, Figure 6 examines training time versus generalization, and Figure 7 tracks iterations per layer during language training. Longer-sequence robustness is also examined. The copying ablation in Table 1, sequential-versus-parallel comparison and modular-arithmetic iteration sweep are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds for state tracking and copying and retain the same uncertainty values in Table 1. No changed uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence-interval practice or significance testing is documented.

E6.justification: Table 2 updates the proposed two-layer, four-reflection modular-arithmetic result from 0.280 to 0.384 and adds GatedDeltaProduct at 0.342; the other baseline values remain unchanged. v2 also adds substantial mixer, long-sequence, timing and language-modeling results, including lower FineWeb validation perplexity for FP-Mamba than Mamba. These are updated or new results; architecture and protocol revisions prevent treating all differences as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The contraction, descent-direction and low-rank expressivity results largely remain, including v1 Appendix D as v2 Appendix F. v2 removes the separate selectivity-memory theorem and proof from v1 Theorem 4.1/Appendix C and the standalone Householder-factorization theorem. It also corrects the Neumann-series bound to use the inverse of I minus Lambda. These prune and correct supporting theory without replacing the theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The central claims remain: represent dense RNNs through fixed points of diagonal RNNs, trade computation for expressivity at fixed parameter count, and combine state tracking with memory. Both abstracts retain state-of-the-art claims on the same four toy tasks. v2's contribution list emphasizes stability and nonlinear feedback already developed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of task-dependent computation, language-modeling gains beyond repeated depth, and FP-Mamba2 generalization through improved recall. It explicitly discusses weaker guarantees for time-varying parametrizations and acknowledges that output normalization does not guarantee contraction. Conversely, v1's selectivity-induced recency-bias and low-rank-collapse explanations disappear. The nonunique-fixed-point limitation and copying-position mechanism are retained.

D1.justification: v2 provides new mixer implementation formulas, Kronecker eigenvalue normalization using power iteration, and stopping/damping details. It adds language-model dimensions, optimizer settings, accumulation steps, four A100-80GB GPUs and a plainLM implementation reference. State-tracking sampling is described more fully. Reproducibility remains limited by conflicting gate descriptions and training-step totals inconsistent with the stated epoch count.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and connections to stable RNN parametrizations, including Arjovsky and Helfrich, recurrent backpropagation, Neural ODEs and newer expressivity work. It specifically relates its factorization to Helfrich et al. and adds FineWeb/plainLM references. References such as Fung's Jacobian-free backpropagation and Urías are removed. The broad positioning against diagonal RNNs and existing implicit models remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and background are extensively rewritten, and the method, memory discussion and evaluation are reorganized. Related work, copying derivations and several experimental discussions move into structured appendices. The title changes, and Bedouin is renamed FP-Mamba throughout.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a predominantly single-column layout, adds an appendix contents page and replaces the detailed architecture sketch with a simpler framework schematic. Comparison figures separate model variants from baselines, and new timing, language-modeling and long-sequence panels substantially expand the visual presentation. Existing convergence figures and theoretical diagrams are retained with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 better grounds the practical computation tradeoff through same-hardware timing in Figure 6 and FineWeb perplexity and iteration measurements in Figures 7–8, extending v1's toy-task evidence. New mixer comparisons and stronger baselines also improve empirical assessment. However, Section 4.3 claims hidden dependence for all components while Appendix C.2 retains original Mamba gating, and Appendix D.2 gives inconsistent training-step totals. These reporting problems limit the otherwise useful gains in evidence and explanation.
